record.narrative: Initial screen: feature_002, feature_034, and feature_060 are complete binary predictors with roughly balanced exposure/comparator counts, so Welch comparisons should have good power and satisfy the minimum-cell-count rule. They are tested against four representative outcomes: outcome_012 as a typical CRISPR dependency score; outcome_001 because it has a more negative mean dependency and larger spread; outcome_014 because it appears more heterogeneous; and outcome_006 because it also has broad dispersion. Directions are left uncertain because predictor labels are opaque and no reliable prior mechanistic direction is available. For these representative outcomes, a clinically meaningful difference is approximately a 10% relative shift in dependency score; with typical means near -0.25 to -0.42, this corresponds to absolute differences around 0.02-0.04, except outcome_014's near-zero mean will require extra caution when interpreting relative significance. These tests are association/hypothesis-generating, not causal claims.

Run the complete registered initial screen: feature_002, feature_034, and feature_060 each compared as exposed=1 versus comparator=0 across the four representative outcomes. These are balanced complete binary predictors, so discovery Welch tests should have adequate cell counts. This broad screen will allocate later effort: strong and clinically meaningful effects across outcomes will justify focused follow-up, while weak or null panels will motivate alternative predictors or more refined subgroup/interaction analyses.

The initial balanced binary screen provides no evidence supporting positive exposed-minus-comparator dependency-score differences. All 12 discovery intervals include zero, and most point estimates are small relative to the approximated 10% clinical threshold. For outcome_012 the threshold is about 0.025 in absolute terms, and the feature_002, feature_034, and feature_060 estimates are near zero. For outcome_001 the threshold is about 0.042, and all three estimates are below that magnitude. For outcome_014 the threshold is smaller, about 0.009, but all three estimates are still below and null-inclusive. For outcome_006, feature_002 and feature_060 have raw negative point estimates around 0.019-0.021, which are near the approximate 10% threshold, but their 95% intervals are wide and include zero; because the registered claims were positive-direction claims, these results do not support acceptance. They are hypothesis-generating only and motivate separate negative-direction follow-up rather than validation of the original positive claims. The initial feature_034 outcome_006 estimate is smaller and also null-inclusive. I therefore reject all 12 registered positive claims and close this initial panel. The next proposals test two additional complete binary predictors, feature_008 and feature_045, across the same representative outcomes, and register two reversed outcome_006 claims for feature_002 and feature_060 as exploratory follow-ups to the observed negative point estimates. No validation is requested because there is no accepted claim or sufficiently precise evidence of clinical significance yet.

No new validation results or response deadlines are currently listed, so there is no new independent evidence to incorporate. The active scientific status is unchanged: the initial 12 positive-direction screen claims (H1-H12) were rejected because all discovery intervals included zero and none demonstrated a clinically meaningful exposed-minus-comparator difference under the original positive-direction hypotheses. The two reversed outcome_006 follow-ups (H21 and H22) remain unresolved: their signed point estimates are slightly above the approximate 10% relative threshold for outcome_006 (about 0.0175 absolute), but their 95% intervals include zero, so they are hypothesis-generating rather than supported findings. The next priority is to analyze the registered feature_008 and feature_045 comparisons (H13-H20). If those also fail to produce clinically meaningful differences with intervals excluding zero, I will expand to other complete predictors or carefully chosen categorical contrasts, while keeping any reversed claims separate from post-hoc screening results. All current conclusions remain dataset associations, not causal claims or generalizable claims.

This exploration adds a second broad binary screen using three complete predictors with adequate exposure cell sizes: feature_042 (exposed proportion about 0.23), feature_020 (about 0.17), and feature_065 (about 0.20). These predictors are not duplicated in earlier active claims and are tested against the same four representative outcomes so that promising associations can be compared across outcomes with low-noise outcome_012, broader-dispersion outcome_006, higher-threshold outcome_001, and heterogeneous near-zero-mean outcome_014. Directions are left uncertain because the predictor labels are opaque; a positive claim corresponds to higher dependency score after exposure, while a negative estimate would correspond to stronger dependency after exposure. The relative clinical threshold is roughly 0.025 for outcome_012, 0.018 for outcome_006, 0.042 for outcome_001, and 0.009 for outcome_014, but outcome_014 is interpreted cautiously because its mean is close to zero. I also register two interaction refinements of the unresolved negative-direction outcome_006 follow-ups for feature_002 and feature_060. These test whether the outcome_006 contrast differs when the other balanced binary predictor is present, which could clarify whether the two near-threshold negative signals are independent effects or modified by each other. These remain association/hypothesis-generating tests in this dataset.

I am requesting the eight pending feature_008 and feature_045 representative-outcome comparisons first because they complete the second balanced complete-predictor screen. I also select feature_042 on outcome_012 and outcome_006 to begin assessing whether a different exposure prevalence predicts dependency scores, while reserving capacity for effect modification: the feature_002-by-feature_060 and feature_060-by-feature_002 interactions on outcome_006 refine the two unresolved negative-direction follow-ups. These interactions test whether the near-threshold outcome_006 main-effect signals are independent or depend on the other binary predictor. All selected cells are expected to meet the minimum observation requirement, and results will be judged by signed effect size, 95% interval, and approximate 10% clinical threshold.

Most of the newly delivered feature_008, feature_045, and feature_042 representative-outcome comparisons do not support clinically meaningful positive exposed-minus-comparator differences. For outcome_012, the approximate 10% absolute threshold is about 0.025; H13, H17, and H23 have point estimates well below that threshold and null-inclusive intervals, so the positive-direction claims are rejected and closed. For outcome_001, the threshold is about 0.042; H14 and H18 are small and not sufficiently precise, with H18 particularly below the clinical threshold, so those positive claims are rejected. For outcome_014, where the near-zero mean makes relative significance less stable, H15 rejects the positive feature_008 claim, while H19 for feature_045 has a clinically sized positive point estimate but a wide interval that includes zero and small effects; because it is null-inclusive and arose in a screened predictor with inconsistent results across other outcomes, I leave it unresolved and deferred rather than accepting. For outcome_006, H16 and H20 do not support positive feature_008 or feature_045 effects and are closed. H23 remains the only clear signal in this batch, but it is in the opposite direction from the registered positive claim: raw exposed-minus-comparator difference is about -0.053, consistent with stronger dependency in the feature_042-exposed group. That is clinically large relative to the outcome_006 mean (roughly 30%), and the 95% interval excludes zero in the negative direction. I therefore reject the original positive H24 claim, but I do not close the scientific question because this is the first interval-excluding-zero signal. Given multiple screened comparisons, a Bonferroni-like sensitivity check would likely weaken the 95% discovery interval, and the lower bound of the reversed-direction magnitude is below the 10% clinical threshold. I request independent validation of the H24 underlying comparison to determine whether the negative feature_042 association on outcome_006 is robust. I register a reversed negative-direction refinement of this comparison rather than accepting H24 as originally written. The interaction claims H33 and H34 are identical and null-inclusive, indicating no evidence that the feature_002-by-feature_060 interaction explains the weak outcome_006 signals; consequently H21 and H22 are deferred as post-hoc unresolved follow-ups rather than validated now.

The new independent validation result R25 resolves the feature_042 outcome_006 question negatively for both the originally registered positive claim H24 and the reversed negative refinement H35. For H24, the validation estimate is +0.0067 with a conservative independent interval from -0.0520 to +0.0653. This interval includes zero, and the point estimate is far from any clinically meaningful positive exposed-minus-comparator difference. Therefore the original positive H24 claim is rejected and the comparison is closed. For the reversed claim H35, the same validation is signed as -0.0067 with interval -0.0653 to +0.0520. Although discovery evidence R22 showed a clinically sized raw negative difference of about -0.053, the validation point estimate is near zero and opposite in direction to the discovery raw effect, and the interval includes zero. Because the independent validation was requested specifically to test whether the discovery signal would replicate, and it does not, I reject and close H35 as well. This means the apparent stronger outcome_006 dependency associated with feature_042 exposure in discovery is not supported as a reliable dataset association after independent validation. The H25 and H26 outcome_001/outcome_014 feature_042 comparisons remain untested but are deferred as lower priority because the primary feature_042 signal failed replication. Current supported findings: none. Negative findings: broad balanced binary screens using feature_002, feature_034, feature_060, feature_008, feature_045, feature_042, and the feature_002-by-feature_060 interaction did not provide accepted evidence for clinically meaningful differences in the representative outcomes. The H19 feature_045/outcome_014 estimate remains unresolved and deferred because it is clinically sized in point estimate but null-inclusive and inconsistent across other outcomes. The most informative next analysis is to finish the pending feature_020 and feature_065 representative screens, add the remaining feature_065 outcomes, and start two new complete binary predictors, feature_050 and feature_021, across the same representative outcomes. These predictors have adequate exposure prevalence and provide broad follow-up without repeatedly chasing the failed feature_042 signal. All conclusions remain dataset-specific associations and do not establish causality or generalizability.

There are currently no accepted claims, and the main evidence is a set of null or nonreplicated screening comparisons. The next scientifically useful wave is to broaden beyond the binary feature_020/feature_065/feature_050/feature_021 panel that remains pending, while adding a nominal categorical predictor with adequate cell counts. Feature_054 is the safest multilevel variable available because the nonmajority level is known to have 578 observations versus 1422 for the majority level, so a level_002-versus-level_001 contrast should satisfy the minimum-cell rule. I also add two additional complete binary predictors, feature_012 and feature_037, whose exposed counts are approximately 376 and 411 respectively, providing adequate comparison cells and nontrivial exposure prevalence. All new claims use negative direction because the biological hypothesis is that the exposed category marks stronger CRISPR dependency, which corresponds to a raw exposed-minus-comparator difference moving more negative. The alternative hypotheses are null or opposite-direction, namely the exposed category marks weaker dependency or no clinically meaningful difference. I test these on the same representative outcomes to preserve interpretability: outcome_012 has a relatively low-noise dependency scale with an approximate 10% absolute threshold around 0.025; outcome_006 is a higher-dispersion outcome with a threshold around 0.0175; outcome_001 is a more negative dependency score with a threshold around 0.0415; and outcome_014 is near zero in mean, so any relative-significance interpretation is made cautiously. These remain association hypotheses in the supplied dataset only; none is a causal or generalizability claim. If any new comparison has a clinically sized signed estimate with an interval excluding zero, it should be considered for independent validation rather than accepted on a single post-hoc screening result. If the results are again small or null-inclusive, these predictors will be closed and the next exploration should shift toward carefully selected categorical levels with known adequate counts, subgroup refinement only after a robust main effect, or a different modeling angle that is not repeated post-hoc reversal of screened signals.

I am selecting complete representative-outcome panels for three predictors that are currently untested and scientifically complementary: feature_020 (H27-H30), feature_065 (H31, H32, H36, H37), and the nominal categorical contrast feature_054 level_002 versus level_001 (H46-H49). This uses all twelve analysis slots to complete two already registered binary predictors and to introduce one categorical predictor with adequate cell counts. The complete-panel design is more informative than isolated outcome tests because it lets us distinguish outcome-specific associations from broad dependency-score associations: outcome_012 provides a lower-noise representative dependency scale, outcome_006 has higher dispersion and a lower absolute 10% threshold, outcome_001 has a more negative mean and a larger absolute 10% threshold, and outcome_014 is near zero so its relative threshold must be interpreted cautiously. Feature_054 is also useful because it expands the search beyond binary indicators; level_002 has about 578 observations, so the level_002-versus-level_001 contrast should satisfy the minimum cell-size rule. I am not selecting the previously failed feature_042 follow-ups or the deferred post-hoc reversed signals because replication was not supported. I am also postponing additional binary panels (feature_050, feature_021, feature_012, feature_037) unless these three panels produce a clinically sized, interval-excluding-zero candidate. The selected comparisons remain dataset-association hypotheses; none will be interpreted as causal or generalizable without further evidence.

The new feature_020, feature_065, and feature_054 representative panels mostly provide null or wrong-direction evidence for the registered hypotheses. For outcome_012, the approximate 10% absolute scale threshold is about 0.025. H27 and H31 have raw differences in the negative direction and, in any case, are not supported by intervals excluding zero. H46 tests the feature_054 level_002-versus-level_001 negative-dependency hypothesis; its signed estimate is +0.0052, implying a raw level_002-minus-level_001 difference of only -0.0052, well below the clinical threshold and imprecise. Therefore those claims are rejected and closed. For outcome_006, the approximate 10% threshold is about 0.0175. H32 and H47 are small and null-inclusive, so the feature_065 and feature_054 positive or negative claims are rejected. H28 is the only new candidate that crosses the clinical-size threshold in the registered direction: the signed estimate is +0.0407, about 23% of the outcome_006 mean magnitude, but the 95% interval includes zero, from -0.0079 to +0.0894. Because it is not statistically supported in discovery and arose in a multiplicity-heavy screen, I do not accept it. I request independent validation of H28 rather than closing it, because it is the strongest currently eligible dataset signal and replication would materially inform whether feature_020 marks weaker dependency for this outcome. For outcome_001, the approximate 10% threshold is about 0.042; H29, H36, and H48 are below the registered-direction clinical threshold or wrong in direction and have intervals that include zero, so they are rejected and closed. For outcome_014, the mean is near zero, making relative thresholds less stable. H30 is small and null-inclusive; H37 is wrong in direction for the positive claim although the raw negative difference is moderately large, it is not precise; H37 is therefore rejected as written. H49 is wrong in direction for the negative-dependency claim and null-inclusive. I do not register post-hoc opposite-direction refinements now because feature_042 showed that such screening reversals can fail replication, and none of these opposite-direction effects currently has an interval excluding zero in the new data. All conclusions remain associations in the supplied dataset only, not causal claims.

The independent validation results close the current candidate set. For H28, feature_020 exposure versus non-exposure on outcome_006, the discovery signed estimate was +0.0407 with a null-inclusive 95% interval. Independent validation R38 gave a signed estimate of -0.0230 with interval [-0.0902, +0.0443]. The validation point is opposite the registered positive hypothesis and the interval contains zero, so H28 is rejected and closed. This also closes the feature_020 lead for this outcome. For H12, feature_060 exposure versus non-exposure on outcome_006, validation R39 is signed +0.0253 with interval [-0.0267, +0.0773]. The point estimate exceeds the approximate 10% outcome_006 clinical scale of 0.0175, but it is not precise and the interval crosses zero and clinically meaningful negative values. Therefore H12 is rejected and closed. The reversed negative claim H22 is also rejected and closed because the same validation is signed -0.0253 under the negative hypothesis, interval [-0.0773, +0.0267]; the raw direction is not in support and the interval is null-inclusive. I additionally close the related post-hoc feature_002 reversal H21 and the deferred feature_045/outcome_014 comparison H19: their discovery point estimates are at best borderline or clinically sized in point estimate, but intervals include zero and the predictor patterns are inconsistent across outcomes. Together with the earlier failure of feature_042 on outcome_006, the evidence so far does not support an accepted dataset association. The main negative conclusion is that multiple screened binary predictors and the representative outcome_006 high-dispersion candidates are not reproducible under conservative independent validation. The next most informative step is to finish the already registered representative panels for feature_050, feature_021, feature_012, and feature_037, prioritizing outcome_012 because it is low-noise, while using outcome_006/outcome_001/outcome_014 for specificity. I also register moderate-prevalence binary predictors feature_011, feature_052, and feature_027 as new negative-direction exploratory panels for the hypothesis that exposure marks stronger CRISPR dependency. Acceptance will require a clinically sized point estimate with an interval excluding zero, ideally followed by validation for borderline discoveries. These remain dataset association conclusions only, not causal or generalizable claims.

No claims are currently accepted, and the strongest earlier candidates have failed independent validation or remain null-inclusive. To avoid repeated post-hoc chasing of failed binary signals, I register a new complete representative panel for three previously untested complete binary predictors chosen for adequate nonmajority-cell counts: feature_007 exposes the 10.3% group (about 206 exposed versus 1794 comparator); feature_047 exposes the 0.0 nonmajority group (about 383 versus 1617); and feature_023 exposes the 0.0 nonmajority group (about 235 versus 1765). The scientific hypothesis is that the less common biological state marks stronger CRISPR dependency, so the raw exposed-minus-comparator dependency score should be more negative; therefore the claim direction is -1 and anticipated_direction is -1. The alternative is null or opposite direction, namely that the exposed state marks weaker dependency or is not clinically associated. The outcome panel is outcome_012, outcome_015, outcome_006, and outcome_001. outcome_012 and outcome_015 are relatively low-dispersion dependency scales with approximate 10% absolute thresholds near 0.025; outcome_006 is high-dispersion with a lower absolute 10% threshold near 0.0175; outcome_001 has a more negative mean and a larger absolute threshold near 0.0415. I omit outcome_014 in this new wave because its mean is near zero, making relative 10% interpretation unstable. A signed clinically sized estimate with an interval excluding zero would justify focused validation; otherwise these predictors should be closed. All conclusions are associations in the supplied dataset only, not causal or generalizable claims.

No claims are currently accepted, so I use the twelve analysis slots to complete three newly registered, complete negative-direction panels for less-common biological states: feature_007 exposed=1, feature_047 exposed=0, and feature_023 exposed=0. This tests the focused dataset-association hypothesis that the exposed group has a more negative CRISPR dependency score, i.e., stronger dependency. Each predictor panel is run on outcome_012, outcome_015, outcome_006, and outcome_001. outcome_012 and outcome_015 are relatively low-dispersion dependency scales, providing a more stable clinical-scale screen, while outcome_006 and outcome_001 add higher-dispersion or different dependency-scale specificity checks. I do not use outcome_014 in this wave because its mean is near zero and relative 10% interpretation is less stable. The cell counts for all nonmajority groups satisfy the minimum-cell rule: feature_007 has about 206 exposed, feature_047 has about 383 exposed, and feature_023 has about 235 exposed. If any panel yields a signed effect at least near the approximate 10% absolute clinical threshold with an interval excluding zero, it will be considered for focused validation rather than accepted on a single screen. If the panels are small or null-inclusive, these predictors will be closed and the next analysis should move to other registered predictors or to categorical contrasts rather than post-hoc reversal of these null results.

This wave tests whether less-common binary states mark stronger CRISPR dependency, operationalized as a negative exposed-minus-comparator dependency score. Approximate absolute 10 percent clinical thresholds are about 0.025 for outcome_012 and outcome_015, about 0.0175 for outcome_006, and about 0.0415 for outcome_001. For feature_007, H70 and H71 are small and null inclusive, so they are rejected and closed. H72 is the key new direction reversal: under the registered negative direction the signed estimate is -0.0642 with signed interval [-0.1211, -0.0074], meaning the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast is positive by about 0.064 on outcome_006 and the signed interval is entirely on the wrong side of zero. This raw magnitude is clinically large for outcome_006, but it is evidence against H72 as written, so H72 is rejected and closed. I do not accept a post-hoc reversal from a multiplicity-heavy screen; instead I register a positive-direction refinement for the same raw contrast so future evidence can be correctly signed. H73 is the same predictor on outcome_001 and has a similar raw positive point estimate, but its interval includes zero, so it is rejected and closed as written and does not alone justify a reversal. For feature_047, H74 through H77 are small, wrong direction, or null inclusive, so all are rejected and closed. For feature_023, H78 and H79 are not clinically supported in the registered direction and are rejected and closed. H80 and H81 are the main borderline correct-direction leads: both have signed point estimates above the relevant clinical thresholds, but their 95 percent intervals include zero. I do not accept them from this discovery screen. H80 is the stronger relative outcome_006 signal, so I request independent validation of H80 and keep it active pending replication; H81 remains deferred unresolved. No claim is accepted now, and all statements remain dataset associations only, not causal or generalizable claims.

The response-deadline claim H24 tests a positive exposed-minus-comparator difference for feature_042 exposure versus non-exposure on outcome_006. Its direct discovery evidence R22 was actually in the opposite raw direction: under the positive claim the signed estimate is negative and the discovery interval excludes zero, which is evidence against the positive claim rather than support for it. The independent validation R25 for the same positive claim is near zero, with a very wide interval containing zero and clinically relevant positive and negative values. Therefore the original H24 claim remains rejected and closed. This also reinforces the earlier closure of the feature_042 negative-direction refinement H35: a strong but direction-reversed discovery signal failed independent validation, so it should not be accepted.

The new validation for H80 concerns feature_023, where the exposed group is the less common 0 state versus the comparator 1 state, with the registered hypothesis that the exposed group has stronger dependency, i.e. a negative raw contrast. Under the negative-direction claim, discovery R50 was correctly signed and clinically sized in point estimate, but the 95 percent interval included zero. Independent validation R52 was also correctly signed, with a signed estimate of about 0.027, which exceeds the approximate absolute 10 percent scale for outcome_006, but its independent interval is wide and null-inclusive: [-0.0439, 0.0969]. This validation does not exclude zero and does not exclude clinically meaningful opposite-direction values. Consequently H80 is rejected and closed.

I also reassess the related feature_023/outcome_001 claim H81. Its discovery-only evidence R51 had a clinically sized point estimate but a null-inclusive interval. Given that the primary feature_023/outcome_006 lead failed independent validation, and there is no independent support for the outcome_001 secondary contrast, H81 is best treated as a negative/unsupported discovery-only signal and closed. No feature_023 claim is accepted.

The main active lead is now H82, the correctly signed positive refinement for feature_007 versus comparator on outcome_006. Its direct discovery evidence R42 is clinically large and has a discovery interval excluding zero, implying a raw positive difference of about 0.064 for outcome_006. However, this is a post-hoc reversal from a multiplicity-heavy screen, and analogous direction-reversed discovery signals have already failed independent validation. The lower discovery bound is also below the clinical-size threshold, so the evidence is suggestive but not enough to justify acceptance before replication. H82 therefore remains unresolved and active, and the next most informative validation request should target H82 if allowed. If it fails validation, the feature_007/outcome_006 reversal should be closed.

The current accepted set remains empty. The next scientific step is twofold: validate H82 rather than accepting it from a single reversed discovery signal, and continue broad completion of registered representative panels for untested binary predictors, prioritizing low-noise outcomes outcome_012 and outcome_015 while using outcome_006 and outcome_001 for specificity. I registered new less-common-state binary panels for feature_030 and feature_022, both with negative direction and expected raw negative contrast, to test whether the less common biological state marks stronger CRISPR dependency without chasing previously observed reversed effects. All conclusions remain associations in the supplied dataset only, not causal or generalizable claims.

No claims are accepted, and several prior binary predictors have failed validation or remain null-inclusive. The most useful next comparisons are: (1) test whether the active feature_007 positive outcome_006 lead generalizes to another dependency scale or is outcome-specific, and (2) move from low-prevalence binary screens to higher-count categorical contrasts with better statistical power on untested outcomes.

Feature_007 exposed=1 versus 0 shows a positive raw contrast on outcome_006 in H82: signed +0.0642, interval +0.0074 to +0.1211. The prior negative claim H73 on outcome_001 was rejected as written, but its raw evidence is positive: signed -0.0483 under negative direction corresponds to raw approximately +0.0483, with a null-inclusive interval. I therefore register a correctly signed positive refinement on outcome_001. If feature_007=1 marks weaker dependency on outcome_006, a coherent secondary outcome_001 positive signal would support a broader association; if it is absent or opposite, the outcome_006 effect is more likely outcome-specific or fragile. I also register a positive interaction contrast for feature_007 against 0 on outcome_006 within feature_034=1 versus complement, to characterize whether any validated positive effect is concentrated in a common binary context. This remains unresolved and should only receive emphasis after H82 validation.

For broader exploration, I register categorical predictor panels where the compared groups are likely hundreds of observations rather than low-prevalence binary groups. Approximate 10% absolute clinical thresholds for the chosen low-dispersion dependency scores are about 0.025 for outcome_005, outcome_002, outcome_016, outcome_013, and outcome_004. For feature_063, level_001 is the most common label (1190 observations), and non-dominant levels likely have several hundred observations each; I test both level_002 and level_003 versus level_001 on outcome_005 and level_002 versus level_001 on outcome_002. For feature_055, level_003 is the most common label (519 observations) in a roughly four-level predictor; I test alternative levels level_001 and level_002 versus level_003 on outcome_016, outcome_013, and outcome_004. The falsifiable scientific hypothesis is that an alternative categorical level marks stronger CRISPR dependency, producing a more negative exposed-minus-comparator dependency score, hence direction -1. Alternatives are null or opposite direction, where the exposed level marks weaker dependency or no clinically meaningful association. These categorical claims are not accepted before evidence; any clinically sized signed estimate with interval excluding zero would justify validation. All statements remain dataset associations only, not causal or generalizable conclusions.

No claims are currently accepted, so I prioritize discovery analyses with the best statistical power and the least dependence on previously failed low-prevalence binary screens. The six categorical contrasts H93-H98 are selected because they compare nominal categories likely containing hundreds of observations per cell and cover untested dependency-score outcomes outcome_005, outcome_002, outcome_016, outcome_013, and outcome_004. These have better power for detecting approximately 10% relative-scale differences than very rare binary exposures. For binary predictors, I select two roughly 20%-prevalence predictors, feature_050 and feature_037, and run each on outcome_012, outcome_006, and outcome_001. Outcome_012 is the primary low-dispersion dependency score and the most interpretable screen; outcome_006 and outcome_001 provide specificity checks on different dependency scales. I do not include the outcome_014 claims in this run because its mean is close to zero, making relative 10% interpretation and small absolute clinical thresholds less stable. I also do not spend slots on the feature_007 interaction H92 in this batch, because the more informative follow-up for feature_007 is independent validation of the primary outcome_006 lead H82 in appraise, rather than an exploratory interaction. The resulting twelve analyses test newly registered high-count categorical hypotheses together with representative 20%-prevalence binary predictors, while avoiding repeated post-hoc chasing of closed or low-prevalence reversed signals. All requested analyses are dataset associations only.

The newly delivered categorical panels provide little support for the registered hypothesis that non-dominant categorical levels mark stronger dependency. H93-H98 are all close to zero and have intervals including zero; their signed estimates are also below the approximate 10% absolute-scale thresholds for the low-dispersion dependency scores. Therefore each is rejected and closed. The feature_037 contrasts H54-H56 are similarly small and null inclusive, so all are rejected and closed. For feature_050, the outcome_012 and outcome_006 screens H38-H39 are null inclusive and small in absolute terms, so the positive-direction claims are rejected and closed. The important exception is H40 on outcome_001: R61 is signed negative with an interval entirely on the wrong side of zero and an effect far larger than the approximate clinical threshold. Because H40 was registered in the positive direction, this evidence contradicts H40 as written and must be assessed as reject. However, the raw implication is clinically major: feature_050=1 may be associated with a much more negative outcome_001 dependency score, i.e., stronger dependency. This is a post-hoc reversal from a multiplicity-heavy screen and an unusually large association, so I register a correctly signed negative refinement and request independent validation of the same raw contrast using H40 as the eligible validation target. If independent validation remains strongly negative, the reversal should be accepted; if it weakens or becomes inconsistent, the feature_050/outcome_001 signal should be closed as a possible discovery artifact or leakage-sensitive outlier. H82 remains active as a secondary unresolved lead. All statements are dataset associations only, not causal or generalizable claims.

The validation for H40 is decisive against the originally registered positive-direction claim. H40 predicted feature_050=1 to have a higher, i.e. less negative, outcome_001 CRISPR dependency score than feature_050=0. Both discovery R61 and independent validation R65, signed to the positive H40 direction, are approximately -0.78 to -0.79 with intervals far below zero. Therefore the raw exposed-minus-comparator difference is strongly negative, implying much stronger dependency in the feature_050=1 group. H40 remains rejected and is now closed. The correctly signed negative refinement H99 has both discovery and independent validation evidence aligned with this reversal: its signed estimates are about +0.784 and +0.793, with validation interval about [0.763, 0.822] under an alpha level accounting for the run's validation multiplicity. This is far beyond the clinically meaningful scale for outcome_001 and replicates independent of the discovery interval. I therefore accept H99 as a dataset association: feature_050=1 versus feature_050=0 is associated with a substantially more negative outcome_001 dependency score. I close H99 as accepted evidence and do not interpret it as causal or generalizable.

The response-deadline validations also close older leads. H28 on feature_020 and outcome_006 had only a null-inclusive discovery signal and was followed by independent validation R38 in the opposite direction with a wide interval containing zero, so H28 remains rejected and closed. H12 on feature_060 and outcome_006 had discovery evidence in the wrong direction and validation R39 that is positive but wide and null-inclusive; therefore H12 remains rejected and closed. No feature_020 or feature_060 claim is supported.

The most important unresolved question is whether accepted H99 is specific to outcome_001 or reflects a broader dependency phenotype. The earlier feature_050 contrasts on outcome_012 and outcome_006 were small and null inclusive, suggesting possible outcome specificity, but several low-dispersion untested outcomes remain. I registered a negative-direction panel for feature_050=1 versus 0 on outcome_015, outcome_016, outcome_005, outcome_009, outcome_010, outcome_007, outcome_013, and outcome_004. A clinically sized negative contrast on additional outcomes would support broader dependency association; null contrasts would refine H99 as an outcome_001-specific dataset association. H82 remains secondary unresolved until later validation or stronger supporting evidence.

The accepted claim H99 identifies a very large, independently validated negative association between feature_050=1 and outcome_001 dependency. The highest-value next step is to determine whether this is an outcome_001-specific dataset association or part of a broader dependency phenotype, and whether it is robust within common subgroups or concentrated in a subgroup. I therefore register negative-direction feature_050 contrasts for the remaining untested outcomes with interpretable low-to-moderate noise: outcome_002, outcome_003, outcome_008, and outcome_011. The falsifiable hypothesis is that feature_050=1 marks stronger CRISPR dependency across multiple dependency scores, producing a raw exposed-minus-comparator difference that is more negative; alternatives are null, outcome-specificity, or an opposite weaker-dependency pattern. I also include feature_050 on outcome_014 because it remains the only untested outcome for the main predictor, but mark anticipated direction uncertain because outcome_014 has a near-zero mean and its relative-scale interpretation is less stable. Approximate 10% absolute scales are about 0.026 for outcome_002, 0.025 for outcome_003, 0.028 for outcome_008, 0.030 for outcome_011, and 0.025 for outcome_012; outcome_001 is much larger in scale but the accepted H99 effect is far above any plausible clinical threshold.

For robustness and heterogeneity, I register a direct subgroup mean_difference for feature_050 on outcome_001 within feature_034=1 and an interaction contrast against feature_002=1 versus its complement. The subgroup mean tests whether the accepted negative association persists in a common half-population context; expected raw direction remains negative if the finding is not an artifact of the feature_034 complement. The interaction has no strong prior direction and is used only to test whether the feature_050 association is more negative in feature_002=1 than in the complement; alternatives are no modification or the opposite context dependence. These remain associations within the supplied dataset, not causal or generalizable statements.

For independent broad exploration, I register safe high-count categorical contrasts from feature_063 and feature_055 on outcome_012 and outcome_001. These use known adequate cell sizes from prior evidence and test levels/outcome combinations not yet examined. The expected raw direction under the scientific hypothesis is negative: an alternative nominal level may mark stronger dependency than the comparator level. Prior feature_063 and feature_055 contrasts were null, so anticipated direction is uncertain and null is a strong alternative. If any signed estimate is clinically sized with an interval excluding zero, it would justify follow-up; otherwise it refines the picture that feature_050, not these partially tested categorical predictors, drives the main outcome_001 signal.

I defer no-evidence outcome_014 panels unrelated to feature_050 and the premature feature_007 interaction because outcome_014 has an unstable relative scale and feature_007 should first be settled at its main outcome_006 lead. All new proposals are dataset-association tests only.

The accepted lead H99 establishes a very large negative association between feature_050=1 and outcome_001 dependency. The most important unresolved question is whether this reflects a broad feature_050 dependency phenotype or an outcome_001-specific dataset association. Earlier feature_050 contrasts on outcome_012 and outcome_006 were small and null inclusive, which increases the value of a complete specificity panel. I therefore select the 12 active negative-direction feature_050 contrasts H100 through H111, covering outcome_015, outcome_016, outcome_005, outcome_009, outcome_010, outcome_007, outcome_013, outcome_004, outcome_002, outcome_003, outcome_008, and outcome_011. These are the remaining low-to-moderate dispersion dependency scores with stable approximate 10% absolute-scale thresholds, roughly 0.025 to 0.030 for most of these outcomes and up to about 0.030 for outcome_011. For a negative-direction claim, a clinically meaningful result would be a signed positive exposed-minus-comparator difference, indicating stronger dependency in feature_050=1, with magnitude near or above the approximate 10% threshold and an interval excluding zero.

I defer H112 on outcome_014 because its mean is near zero and the relative 10% clinical threshold is less interpretable; it can be tested later if the feature_050 pattern suggests a broad effect. I also defer the feature_050 subgroup and interaction checks H113 and H114 for now because establishing outcome specificity is more immediately informative: if feature_050 is largely outcome_001-specific, heterogeneity analysis adds less than a second independent outcome panel; if several outcomes are positive, subgroup heterogeneity becomes a more useful follow-up. Similarly, the independent feature_063 and feature_055 categorical screens H115 through H119 are useful broad exploration but have lower priority than resolving the primary accepted predictor. This batch concentrates power on the strongest existing lead and should either support a broader feature_050 association or refine H99 as an outcome_001-specific association. All conclusions remain dataset associations only, not causal or generalizable claims.

The feature_050 specificity panel is mostly uninformative for the hypothesis that the accepted outcome_001 association reflects a broad dependency phenotype. Because these are negative-direction claims, a clinically favorable signal would be a signed positive exposed-minus-comparator difference, indicating that feature_050=1 has a more negative dependency score. Most signed estimates are near zero or in the opposite direction, and all 95% intervals include zero. The approximate 10% absolute-scale thresholds are about 0.025 for most of these outcomes and about 0.030 for outcome_011. The clearest positive but non-significant signals are H104 on outcome_010 (+0.0184, interval [-0.0017, 0.0385]), H100 on outcome_015 (+0.0176, interval [-0.0015, 0.0367]), H108 on outcome_002 (+0.0151, interval [-0.0039, 0.0342]), and H105 on outcome_007 (+0.0118, interval [-0.0074, 0.0310]). Their point estimates are below the approximate clinical threshold, even though their upper bounds exceed it. Given that these are multiple correlated tests of the same predictor, I do not treat any discovery interval as sufficient evidence of a broader feature_050 effect. H101, H102, H103, H106, H107, H109, H110, and H111 are small, null inclusive, and mostly opposite to the hypothesized direction, so I reject and close them. H100, H105, and H108 are unresolved but deferred because they are weaker or less prioritized than H104. H104 is the strongest positive borderline candidate and therefore the most useful claim for one independent validation request. If H104 survives stricter validation and reaches or exceeds clinical-scale evidence, that would reopen a possible broader feature_050 association; if it weakens or fails, the specificity panel should close and the accepted H99 finding should be described as an outcome_001-specific dataset association rather than a broad dependency phenotype. All statements remain associations in this supplied dataset, not causal or generalizable claims.

The new validation results close the main feature_050 follow-up question. H104 was the strongest borderline positive candidate in the feature_050 outcome-specificity panel, but independent validation R78 is null-inclusive and actually opposite to the registered negative-direction claim: the signed estimate is about -0.0048 with interval [-0.0342, 0.0245] at the validation alpha. This is far short of the approximate 10% outcome_010 clinical scale and reverses the discovery signal. I therefore reject and close H104. With H104 failing, and because H100, H105, and H108 have only subclinical point estimates below their approximate 10% absolute-scale thresholds despite discovery intervals that include zero, I reject and close H100, H105, and H108 as well. Together with the earlier null feature_050 contrasts on outcome_012, outcome_006, outcome_016, outcome_005, outcome_009, outcome_013, outcome_004, outcome_003, outcome_008, and outcome_011, the evidence does not support a broad feature_050 dependency phenotype. The accepted H99 finding remains supported, but it should now be interpreted within this dataset as an outcome_001-specific association rather than a multi-outcome dependency marker. H99 is not rejected or modified by these null results because it has both discovery and independent validation evidence with a very large signed effect far above the clinical scale.

The scheduled response-deadline evidence for H80 also remains unsupportive. For H80, feature_023=0 versus 1 on outcome_006, discovery R50 and validation R52 are both null-inclusive. Validation R52 is positive and has a point estimate above the approximate clinical threshold, but its interval [-0.0439, 0.0969] includes zero and extends well below the threshold. Because the interval does not establish either a reliable direction or a clinically meaningful magnitude, H80 remains rejected and closed. The new validation for H55 also strengthens the earlier null conclusion: discovery R63 and validation R79 are small, null-inclusive, and the validation estimate is opposite to the registered direction. H55 remains rejected and closed. No support emerges for feature_037 or feature_023 associations on outcome_006.

The most informative supported conclusion remains the one accepted claim: feature_050=1 versus feature_050=0 is associated with a much more negative outcome_001 CRISPR dependency score, i.e. stronger outcome_001 dependency. This conclusion is supported by H99 with both discovery and independent validation evidence. It should not be interpreted as causal, generalizable beyond the supplied dataset, or indicative of broader CRISPR dependency across outcomes. The next priority is to resolve the secondary feature_007 leads rather than continue feature_050 specificity. H82 has a positive discovery signal on outcome_006, but the interval's lower bound is below the approximate clinical threshold and the feature_007=1 group is relatively small, so independent validation is now more valuable than additional discovery tests. If validation of H82 is positive and clinically sized, it should be assessed together with H91 and the deferred feature_007 interaction H92 to determine whether the association is outcome-specific, broad, or context-dependent. If H82 validation is null or inconsistent, the feature_007 leads should be closed. I am also keeping H113 and H114 active because, with the outcome-specificity question resolved, characterizing the accepted H99 association within feature_034 and feature_002 contexts is the most relevant robustness follow-up for the only supported predictor. All lower-priority untested binary/categorical panels are deferred to keep the next analysis focused on these two scientific follow-ups.

The accepted and independently validated H99 result establishes a very large feature_050=1 versus 0 association with a more negative outcome_001 dependency score. The outcome-specificity panel has now closed the hypothesis of a broad feature_050 dependency phenotype, so the most useful follow-up for the accepted predictor is robustness within common binary contexts: whether the H99 negative association remains in feature_060=1 and feature_002=1, complementing the already active feature_034=1 subgroup H113 and feature_002 interaction H114. I expect raw negative differences in these subgroups if H99 is a stable dataset association rather than an artifact of one population split; alternatives are attenuation, null effect, or context reversal.

The highest-priority secondary lead is feature_007. H82 gives a positive outcome_006 contrast for feature_007=1 versus 0: the signed positive estimate implies a higher, less negative dependency score, i.e. weaker dependency, and the 95% discovery interval excludes zero, though the lower bound is near the approximate 10% clinical scale. H91 gives a borderline positive outcome_001 signal. I therefore register a direct feature_007 outcome-specificity panel for six additional low-to-moderate dispersion outcomes (outcome_002, outcome_003, outcome_004, outcome_005, outcome_007, and outcome_016) with positive direction. If feature_007=1 marks a general weaker-dependency phenotype, clinically sized positive differences with intervals excluding zero should appear on additional outcomes. Null or inconsistent results would support outcome-specificity and make a false discovery or narrow dataset association more plausible.

I also register feature_007 context checks. Direct subgroup means within feature_034=1 and feature_002=1 test whether the feature_007 outcome_006 lead persists in common half-population contexts. The feature_050 interaction tests whether the feature_007 association is modified by the only accepted strong-dependency marker, although feature_050 itself was outcome_001-specific; no direction is anticipated for the interaction beyond no modification versus opposite or stronger modification. These are dataset association tests only and do not imply causality or generalizability.

Finally, I register one independent categorical exploration for feature_036, comparing level_001 with the dominant level_002 on outcome_001. The hypothesis is that the alternative nominal level may mark stronger outcome_001 dependency, hence a raw negative difference; null or opposite patterns are plausible. If cell sizes are insufficient, this comparison should simply be discarded rather than interpreted. Overall, the next batch is designed either to broaden feature_007 and stabilize the feature_050 accepted finding or to refine both to narrower, outcome-specific dataset associations.

I selected 12 newly registered, currently untested analyses that best resolve the two highest-value follow-up questions. First, I test the secondary feature_007 lead with a targeted outcome-specificity and context panel: H120 and H121 examine the outcome_006 association within common feature_034=1 and feature_002=1 contexts; H122 tests whether it is modified by feature_050, the only accepted strong-dependency marker; and H123 through H128 test outcome_002, outcome_003, outcome_004, outcome_005, outcome_007, and outcome_016. These six outcomes have approximate absolute 10% clinical thresholds near 0.025, with outcome_006 lower because its mean is closer to zero. For positive-direction feature_007 claims, clinically meaningful support would require a signed positive difference, indicating a less negative or weaker dependency score in feature_007=1, of at least roughly threshold magnitude and with an interval excluding zero. A coherent pattern would broaden feature_007; mixed or null results would make the existing outcome_006 signal more likely outcome-specific or unstable. Second, I test robustness of the accepted feature_050 effect on outcome_001 within three binary contexts using negative-direction claims: H113 within feature_034=1, H129 within feature_060=1, and H130 within feature_002=1. A signed positive estimate indicates the accepted raw negative association remains in that context; attenuation, null, or a signed negative estimate would indicate context dependence or fragility. I defer H131 because feature_036 level_001 may be sparse and it is lower priority than resolving feature_007 specificity and feature_050 subgroup robustness. I also defer the feature_050 interaction H114 in favor of the direct feature_002=1 subgroup H130, which is more immediately interpretable for robustness. These remain discovery analyses within the supplied dataset only.

The direct feature_050 robustness checks are decisive. H113 (feature_034=1), H129 (feature_060=1), and H130 (feature_002=1) each show very large signed positive estimates for negative-direction claims, with intervals about [0.76,0.82], far above the outcome_001 approximate 10% absolute scale of about 0.0415. These accept as dataset associations and establish that the accepted H99 association is not confined to the complement of these common half-population contexts. I close H114 because the direct subgroup tests answer the robustness question more usefully than the pending interaction.

The feature_007 panel is mixed. H126 on outcome_005 is a new positive-significant discovery: signed estimate +0.0348, interval [0.0091,0.0605]. The point exceeds the approximate 0.025 clinical threshold, but the lower bound is below it and this is an additional outcome test, so I keep it unresolved and active rather than accepting. H121 is the context feature_007=1 versus 0 on outcome_006 within feature_002=1: estimate +0.0938, interval [0.0160,0.1716]. It excludes zero and has a very large point, but its lower bound is slightly below the approximate outcome_006 clinical scale of 0.0175; with multiple feature_007 tests already conducted, this remains active but unresolved. H120 is wide and null-inclusive (exposed n=104), so it is uninformative rather than disconfirming; I defer it. H122 is uninformative and does not support a positive interaction, especially because the critical cell has only 36 observations. H123, H124, H125, H127, and H128 do not support positive feature_007 associations: H123 is small positive and null inclusive; H124, H127, and H128 are negative and small; H125 is borderline opposite (about -0.0249, close to the 0.0255 clinical threshold) and gives essentially no support for a positive claim. I reject and close these as positive-dependency claims. The opposite H125 signal is intriguing but too imprecise to justify a new reversal now.

Because the strongest validated need is to resolve the original feature_007 lead rather than chase post hoc subgroup or outcome signals, I request independent validation of H82. If H82 survives strict validation, H121 and H126 can be assessed as possible extensions. If it fails, the feature_007 panel should remain exploratory or be closed, given the inconsistent panel and multiple-testing risk.

The validation response for H40 confirms the direction of the accepted feature_050 effect and rejects its opposite: for the positive-direction H40 claim on outcome_001, discovery R61 is about -0.784 and validation R65 is about -0.793, both with intervals far below zero and far beyond the approximate 10% outcome_001 absolute scale (~0.0415). Thus H40 remains rejected and closed. The same evidence supports H99 in the opposite, negative-direction claim: feature_050=1 versus feature_050=0 is associated with a substantially more negative outcome_001 dependency score, i.e. stronger outcome_001 dependency, and this association is very large by the supplied-dataset clinical scale.

The central new result is the independent validation of H82, the original feature_007=1 versus feature_007=0 association on outcome_006. Discovery R42 was positive (signed estimate +0.0642, interval [0.0074,0.1211]) and supported a weaker-dependency interpretation for feature_007=1. However, validation R92 reverses and becomes null: signed estimate -0.0086, interval [-0.0907,0.0734]. This is both opposite to the claimed direction and far below the approximate 10% outcome_006 absolute scale (~0.0175). Therefore H82 is rejected and closed. Because H82 was the anchor for the feature_007 follow-up, this failure makes the remaining positive feature_007 signals much less defensible as general dataset associations.

I therefore reassess the active feature_007 leads. H91 (outcome_001 positive association) is rejected and closed: R43 has a point estimate above the approximate clinical scale but its interval crosses zero, so it does not establish a reliable positive association. H120 (outcome_006 within feature_034=1) is rejected and closed: R80 is null inclusive and sparse, with interval [-0.0107,0.1500]. H121 (outcome_006 within feature_002=1) remains technically positive in discovery R81, but its lower interval bound is just below the approximate clinical threshold, the exposed cell is small, and the related overall H82 signal failed independent validation. I leave H121 unresolved but close it as an exploratory subgroup finding rather than treating it as a supported conclusion.

The only remaining feature_007 lead worth independent validation is H126, the positive outcome_005 association (R86: signed estimate +0.0348, interval [0.0091,0.0605]). Its point estimate exceeds the approximate outcome_005 clinical threshold (~0.025), but the lower bound does not, so it is not yet acceptable. If strict validation of H126 is signed positive, excludes zero, and preferably has a lower bound at or above the clinical scale, it could be accepted as a narrow outcome_005-specific dataset association. If validation is null, opposite, or remains nonclinical, the entire feature_007 lead should be closed.

Supported conclusions: feature_050=1 versus feature_050=0 is a very strong outcome_001-specific negative-dependency association (H99), robust within feature_034=1, feature_060=1, and feature_002=1 contexts (H113, H129, H130). Negative conclusions: feature_050 is not supported as a broad multi-outcome dependency phenotype; H40 is rejected; H82 and H91 are rejected; H120 is rejected; several feature_050 outcome-specific panels and feature_007 outcome panels are closed as null or inconsistent. Unresolved uncertainty: H126 may represent an outcome_005-specific feature_007 association but requires validation. The most informative next analysis is independent validation of H126, not further discovery testing of feature_007 or further feature_050 specificity. All conclusions remain dataset associations, not causal or generalizable claims.

The supported evidence so far is narrow and important. H99, with independent validation and robustness across feature_034=1, feature_060=1, and feature_002=1, supports a very strong supplied-dataset association of feature_050=1 versus 0 with a much more negative outcome_001 dependency score. This is clinically meaningful by the approximate outcome_001 10% scale (~0.0415), but it is not evidence for a broad feature_050 dependency phenotype because the feature_050 outcome-specificity panels are null or rejected. Feature_007 is now a much weaker lead: its anchor outcome_006 association failed strict validation, and the remaining H126 outcome_005 discovery signal is positive but only borderline, with a lower bound below the approximate 0.025 clinical scale. The most decision-relevant next step is independent validation of H126, not additional feature_007 discovery panels.

To avoid idling the analysis queue while H126 is resolved, I register an independent discovery panel using predictors that have not been adequately tested on the two most informative outcomes: outcome_001, where the only accepted marker is exceptionally strong, and outcome_005, where the sole active secondary candidate resides. The new proposals compare alternative nominal levels of feature_048 and feature_009 against their dominant levels on outcome_001 and outcome_005. These predictors have large dominant categories, so comparison cells are expected to be adequate. I also activate existing untested claims H64, H116, and H117 for feature_052 and feature_063, prioritizing these because feature_052 has prevalence similar to the accepted feature_050 marker and feature_063 levels are reasonably populated. This yields a compact but diverse panel of potential biomarker associations without retesting failed feature_050 or feature_007 contrasts.

The registered direction is -1 for these exploratory comparisons: this tests whether the non-dominant or positive exposure level is associated with a more negative dependency score. However, anticipated_direction is zero for all because there is no prior directional evidence for these specific predictor-level comparisons. Opposite, attenuated, or null patterns are scientifically plausible. If a new association emerges with a signed estimate above the relevant 10% absolute scale and an interval excluding zero, and especially if the lower bound is at or above the clinical scale, it will merit validation or acceptance as a dataset-specific association. If results are null or merely borderline, they should remain unresolved or be rejected. All conclusions remain associations in the supplied dataset only; none establish causality or generalizability.

I selected the 12 highest-priority active but previously untested claims registered in the immediately preceding exploration. These are: H64 (feature_052=1 vs 0 on outcome_001); H116 and H117 (feature_063 alternative nominal levels versus level_001 on outcome_001); H132 and H133 (feature_048 level_001 or level_002 versus level_003 on outcome_001); H134 and H135 (feature_048 level_001 or level_002 versus level_003 on outcome_005); H136 and H137 (feature_009 level_001 or level_002 versus level_003 on outcome_001); H138 and H139 (feature_009 level_001 or level_002 versus level_003 on outcome_005); and H140 (feature_052=1 vs 0 on outcome_005). All have negative claim direction, so a signed positive estimate would indicate the exposed level is associated with a more negative dependency score, i.e. stronger dependency. Clinically relevant support would require an estimate beyond the approximate outcome-specific 10% scale and an interval excluding zero, with stronger acceptance if the lower bound also exceeds the clinical scale. I do not rerun feature_007 or feature_050 comparisons because those leads are already assessed or accepted, and rerunning would not provide new discovery evidence. I also do not run H126 as a discovery comparison because it already has discovery evidence; resolving its remaining uncertainty should occur through an independent validation request in appraise. This selection therefore broadens the search to independent predictors while preserving the sample needed for the key H126 validation decision.

The independent categorical panel is mostly null, with one genuinely new signal and one unstable extreme.

Nulls: H64 (feature_052=1 on outcome_001, R93 +0.0018 [-0.039,0.042]) and H140 (feature_052 on outcome_005, R104 +0.0014 [-0.019,0.022]) are essentially exactly null, so with the previously untested feature_052 claims (H62, H63, H65) I close the feature_052 thread as unsupported. H134 (feature_048 level_001 on outcome_005, R98 -0.0006) and H135 (level_002, R99 wide null, n=25) are null and closed. H116 (feature_063 level_002 vs level_001 on outcome_001, R94 -0.0074) and H117 (level_003 vs level_001, R95 +0.0208 with a wide interval on n=98) give no clinically meaningful support; H132 (feature_048 level_001 on outcome_001, R96 +0.0330 [-0.008,0.074]) has a sub-clinical point estimate (below the ~0.0415 outcome_001 scale) and an interval crossing zero, so all are rejected and closed. H137/H139 returned invalid cells (n=13) and are closed as untestable, not as evidence of absence.

The one strong new lead is H136: feature_009 level_001 vs level_003 on outcome_001, signed +0.0808, interval [0.0166,0.1449], cells 175/1440. The point is roughly 1.9x the approximate 10% outcome_001 scale and the interval excludes zero, so this is the largest new effect found so far outside the accepted feature_050 result. However, it is a single exploratory hit among a very large number of tests, its lower bound is below the clinical scale, and it overlaps the same outcome where the accepted marker operates. Because the anchor feature_007 lead just failed independent validation after a clean discovery interval, I do not accept H136 on discovery alone; I keep it unresolved and active, and will test its specificity and independence before (or after) validation.

H133 (feature_048 level_002, R97 +0.192 [0.015,0.370]) looks dramatic but has only 25 exposed observations among many rare categorical levels; the interval half-width (~0.18) is 4.3x the clinical scale, and outcome_001 has a long left tail, so the estimate is very plausibly outlier-driven. There is no feasible strict validation split with 20+ observations in that cell, so I close it as unreliable rather than treat it as a candidate association; a registered diagnostic (level_001 vs level_002) will indicate whether level_002 is even distinguishable from the adjacent level.

Validation choice: I request validation of H126 (feature_007=1 on outcome_005, discovery +0.0348 [0.0091,0.0605], exposed n=206). It is the pre-planned decisive step, is well powered enough to yield a clean verdict under strict validation, and it closes the entire feature_007 thread either way (its anchor H82 already failed). Validation of H136 is the next priority once its outcome-specificity panel and feature_0050 independence checks are available, since its n=175 exposed group may not clear the strict validation interval unless the true effect is at the upper end; a specificity/context pattern will make its eventual verdict far more interpretable. Registered for the next analysis: feature_009 level_001 vs level_003 on outcome_012, outcome_015, outcome_002, outcome_006, outcome_004, outcome_014 (specificity: does it mark a broad dependency phenotype or only outcome_001, as feature_050 does?); the same contrast within feature_050=1 and within feature_050=0 (is it independent of, or confounded with, the accepted marker?); and feature_048 level_001 vs level_002 as an artifact check. All statements remain associations in the supplied dataset, with no causal or generalizability claim.

Validation has now closed the feature_007 thread completely. The decisive result is R105 for H126 (feature_007=1 vs 0 on outcome_005): the strict validation estimate is -0.0248 with interval [-0.0654, 0.0157], i.e. it reverses the claimed direction, crosses zero, and its upper bound (0.0157) lies below the approximate 10% outcome_005 clinical scale (~0.025). Combined with the earlier anchor failure (H82 outcome_006: discovery +0.0642 significant, validation -0.0086 null/opposite), this is the second independent strict-validation failure for the same predictor, so the positive discovery signals for feature_007 are not reproducible in held-out data. I reject and close H126. H120 also received validation (R106 +0.0815 [-0.0477, 0.2108]) in the sparse feature_034=1 stratum: the point is positive but the interval is very wide and null-inclusive on ~98 exposed observations, so it neither rescues the lead nor adds evidence; it stays rejected and closed. The remaining feature_007 items (H70-H73, H82, H91, H122-H128, H120, H126) are all rejected/closed; H92 (interaction with feature_034) I close as unresolved because testing it further is no longer informative once the marginal signal has failed replication twice. H121 (outcome_006 within feature_002=1, +0.0938 [0.016,0.172]) remains unresolved and closed: its lower bound sits just below the clinical scale, its exposed cell is only 103, and it belongs to a predictor whose two broader tests both failed validation - subgroup mining is not a basis for acceptance. Two older response deadlines are also resolved and unchanged: H104 (feature_050 on outcome_010) validation is -0.0048 [-0.0342, 0.0245], null and opposite to the claimed direction, confirming the outcome-specificity of the accepted feature_050 effect; H55 (feature_037 on outcome_006) validation is -0.0073 [-0.0727, 0.0581], null, so it remains rejected. The two response deadlines therefore produced no new support anywhere except retrospectively reinforcing H99.

The single surviving lead is H136 (feature_009 level_001 vs level_003 on outcome_001, discovery +0.0808 [0.0166, 0.1449], n=175/1440), roughly 1.9x the outcome_001 10% scale. Given how many discovery tests have been run, and after two replication failures, I will not accept it on discovery alone, but I also recognize that a strict validation split (alpha ~0.0038, expected half-width around 0.08 at n~175) may fail to clear zero even if the association is real. So the decision will be based on the whole internal evidence pattern rather than one more binary test: the registered specificity panel (outcome_012, outcome_015, outcome_002, outcome_006, outcome_004, outcome_014 for the same contrast, H141-H146) and the stratification checks within feature_050=1 and feature_050=0 (H147, H148), plus the feature_048 level_001 vs level_002 artifact check (H149). Acceptance rule: if the feature_050=0 stratum alone shows an estimate near 0.08 with an interval excluding zero, and the outcome panel is null elsewhere (an outcome_001-specific pattern analogous to the accepted feature_050 marker), I will accept H136 as a dataset association and, if budget allows, spend one validation slot on it for confirmation; if the panel shows the effect only in the feature_050=1 stratum, it is likely an artifact of overlap with the accepted marker and will be closed; if estimates are attenuated or erratic across outcomes, it is likely another multiplicity hit and will be rejected.

Because feature_007 is finished, I re-broaden discovery. I reactivate the registered but untested outcome_001 contrasts for six previously untested binary predictors (feature_021 H44, feature_012 H52, feature_011 H60, feature_027 H68, feature_030 H86, feature_022 H90), and register six parallel outcome_005 contrasts plus outcome_001/outcome_005 contrasts for the untested multi-level categorical predictors feature_028, feature_019, and feature_055 (level_001 vs level_003). Prioritized for the informative outcomes (outcome_001, scale ~0.0415; outcome_005, scale ~0.025), this panel searches for additional independent markers rather than re-testing already-failed predictors. All conclusions remain associations in the supplied dataset; nothing here supports causality or generalizability.

The strongest remaining hypothesis is that feature_009 level_001 versus level_003 marks stronger outcome_001 dependency, as in H136 (+0.0808 [0.0166,0.1449]). Because feature_007 failed independent validation twice, I will not accept H136 on discovery alone. I register a refinement of H136 as an interaction contrast: within feature_050=1 versus its complement, the claim direction -1 means a positive signed result would indicate that level_001 is associated with a more negative outcome_001 score more strongly in the feature_050=1 stratum. Expected direction is uncertain. A near-null interaction would support a homogeneous effect across feature_050, a positive interaction would raise concern that the apparent H136 effect is concentrated with or confounded by the accepted feature_050 marker, and a negative interaction would suggest the effect is stronger outside feature_050=1. This complements H147 and H148 by directly assessing effect modification rather than only estimating stratum-specific contrasts. 

I also register an outcome_005 panel for three categorical predictors that already have outcome_001 tests queued: feature_028 level_001 versus level_003, feature_019 level_001 versus level_002, and feature_055 level_001 versus level_003. Each tests whether the named exposed level is associated with a more negative dependency score (direction -1) with no prior directional evidence. A signed estimate at or beyond the approx 0.025 clinical scale for outcome_005 with an interval excluding zero would identify a candidate dataset association; subclinical, reversed, null, or small-cell unstable results would not. These tests are independent of feature_007 and feature_050 and broaden marker discovery on a second informative outcome. 

Finally, I reactivate H41, the already registered feature_050 contrast on outcome_014, to complete the specificity panel for the accepted marker. A null or subclinical result would reinforce that feature_050 is mainly outcome_001-specific, whereas a clinically meaningful effect would materially expand its scope. All proposed comparisons remain associations in the supplied dataset only and support neither causality nor generalizability.

I selected the 12 untested comparisons that best use the current analysis budget. The dominant unresolved lead is H136: feature_009 level_001 versus level_003 on outcome_001, with a signed positive discovery estimate of about 0.0808 and an interval excluding zero. Because the direction is -1, a signed positive estimate means that level_001 is associated with a more negative outcome_001 dependency score, i.e. stronger dependency. I will not rerun H136, because it already has discovery evidence.
